newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Blair - UK should keep EMU options open.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Blair - UK should keep EMU options open.

text.p: British opposition Labour Party leader Tony Blair said on Tuesday Britain's options on a single European currency should remain open. "Our options on a single currency should remain open, to be determined according to our national interest. Any change will only come with the full consent of the people," he said in a speech prepared for delivery at the Labour Party's annual conference in Blackpool.
Blair noted that Britain would have the presidency of the European Union in the first half of 1998, less than a year after the likely date of the general election in May 1997.

"One of our key priorities in that presidency will be the completion of the Single Market," Blair said. "Today I set a deadline: June 1998, the end of the British presidency, for the completion of the Single Market."
Blair said he would begin discussions with other European leaders now, while still in opposition to ensure that deadline could be met.

Blair said his aim was that by the end of the first term of a Labour government, there would be a genuine single market in gas and electricity, telecommunications, public procurement and financial services. "That is the way to get the best out of Europe for Britain."
The Labour leader said that if Britain left Europe or retreated to the sidelines the country would lose its influence and inward investment.
"It would be a disaster for jobs and industry. The Tories glory in perpetual isolation. That's not standing up for Britain. That's betraying British interest," he said.
